home.title: Valheim seeds
home.lead: A Valkyrie drops you by the stones of the tenth world, Hugin the raven gives you his first tip, and Odin gives you a task: put down his enemies, one in each land. Eight lands lie ahead, from the soft <meadows>Meadows</meadows> to the <deepNorth>Deep North</deepNorth>. Valheim never tells you the odds. We do, from your <basics>first steps</basics> to the end. Want it harder? Take on the <challenges>challenges</challenges>. Whichever road you take, every weapon, meal and boss you meet on it waits in the <catalog>catalog</catalog>. And before you set sail, drop your <map>seed on the map</map> and find out if it is <rating>good enough</rating> to grow into Yggdrasil.

meadows.name: Meadows
meadows.hook: Where every game begins: Eikthyr, the hives in the houses you rob, the first pickaxe.

black-forest.name: Black Forest
black-forest.hook: Copper, tin and the Elder, and the trolls that guard all three.

swamp.name: Swamp
swamp.hook: Iron sleeps in the Sunken Crypts, and so do the bones that wake Bonemass.

mountain.name: Mountain
mountain.hook: Silver under the snow, wolves on the slopes, Moder's eggs on the peaks.

plains.name: Plains
plains.hook: Black metal, Fuling villages and the totems Yagluth asks for.

mistlands.name: Mistlands
mistlands.hook: Black cores in the mist, and the Queen beneath it.

ashlands.name: Ashlands
ashlands.hook: A sea that burns your boat, fortresses of the Charred, and Fader.

deep-north.name: Deep North
deep-north.hook: The newest land: Kall waits at its end and calls back every boss before him.

return.idolOnly: From level {from}, at the Forge of Potential: one idol a try, no material. The grey numbers are what the workbench would ask for the level; you never pay them, but a break is counted by them.
return.note: So a break at {top} gives back more than one at {max}, though the item took no more material.

forgeName.title: Nidavellir
forgeName.subtitle: In Norse myth, Nidavellir is the home of the dwarves, where the brothers Sindri and Brokkr forged Thor's hammer Mjölnir. Here it is the place to find the name that forges your item without breaking it.
forgeName.question: How do I raise an item at the Forge of Potential without breaking it?
forgeName.again: A name is no luck charm: a second copy of the same item meets every level on its second try, and can break where the first copy rose. Each copy needs fresh characters of its own.
forgeName.answer: Give the character who presses the button the right name. The forge's first try of an item at a level is decided by the character's name alone, so pick the idol, the item and the step, and take a name whose first try raises it.
forgeName.guide: What goes to the forge, what a try takes and why a name decides it is in the guide
forgeName.names: Names whose first try raises it to level {to}:

how.title: How to raise an item with a name
how.lead: One step, one fresh character with a name from above, written exactly. It takes the item, its idol, the recipe's ingredients and warm clothes from a chest at your base, walks past the station that makes the item, and presses the forge's button once. A name holds for the first try of each item at each level; delete the character and make it again, and its tries start over.
how.why: Why the ingredients: the forge lists only the recipes a character knows, and a fresh one learns a recipe by holding all its ingredients and standing by its station.
how.stepsBefore: Every step, from the stations to the name, is in the guide's section

craftTree.title: Craft tree
craftTree.question: How much wood and ore does my run need?
craftTree.answer: Switch off what you skip; the column counts the raw materials the rest takes, with one station of each kind.

how.bands: Each band is a biome; a card stands in the first biome where it can be made, below what it needs. A line runs from what is needed to what needs it.
how.click: A click switches a card off and everything that needs it, or on and everything it needs. A group's name switches the whole set.
how.stations: A station's level is 1 plus its extensions, any of them. Only the campfire, the spits, the torch, the club, the workbench and the hammer are on at first; switch on what you will make, and the stations and extensions it needs come on with it.
how.quality: The numbers on a card are its quality: picking 3 adds the upgrade materials and the station level it needs.
how.column: The column sums the raw materials of everything on, with the slots and weight to carry them.

island.title: The starting island
island.lead: What a run reaches before its first boat. The Meadows and the Black Forest with their altars belong on it; the Swamp and the Mountain with theirs are a bonus. The best seed holds all four.

howToRead.title: How to read the report
howToRead.where: Every distance in a question comes from a scan of many seeds: it is how far three seeds in four have what the run needs, rounded to ten metres. The count before it is what the run asks for: the eggs for Moder, the totems for Yagluth, the cores for a smelter, a kiln and a pair of portals.
howToRead.colour: The colour of an answer is where your seed stands among the scanned ones. Green: the best quarter, the thing lies nearer than on three seeds in four. Grey: the usual middle half. Red: the worst quarter, or none within the distance at all. A count with no need, such as the oaks or the black cores, is coloured the same way by its own quarters. A boss or trader in the strip is green, outside it red. A grey row with no colour is the same on almost every seed and does not count.
howToRead.score: Each green answer gives a block one point, each grey one half, each red none; a block's number is the share it gets of all its answers, and the seed's number the mean of its blocks.

bugs.title: Bugs
bugs.lead: Why does a Burial Chamber on my seed have other rooms than on a friend's, on the very same seed? Because the game turns each Burial Chamber and Sunken Crypt at random, apart from the seed, and the turn decides its rooms.

crypts.title: Burial Chambers and Sunken Crypts differ on the same seed
crypts.how: The game sets every location down at one of {yaws} turns, {step}° apart, and picks the turn with a random number that the seed does not fix. For most locations the turn changes nothing inside. A Burial Chamber in the Black Forest and a Sunken Crypt in the Swamp are different: the turn shifts the dungeon's generator a little, and the generator's position becomes the seed of the dungeon's rooms.
crypts.cores: So one crypt on one seed has a few possible layouts, each with its own rooms, chests, surtling cores and scrap piles. Which one a world gets is settled when the crypt is first generated, and stays.
crypts.others: Troll caves, frost caves, Infested Mines and the other dungeons are not touched by it: their rooms follow from the seed alone.
crypts.maps: A seed map that shows a single layout for a crypt shows one of its possible layouts. What a world really holds is in its save, once someone has walked in.

loot.title: Why the map's loot is an average
loot.why: Click a dungeon or a camp on the map and its panel lists what it holds. Some numbers there are exact, others are averages, for two reasons: the turn of the crypts above, and chests that roll their contents only when opened. The panel sorts every line into one of three groups.
loot.exact: Stands there. Fixed by the seed: the same in every world made from it, so the number is exact.
loot.overYaws: Stands there, by its turn. What stands in a Burial Chamber or a Sunken Crypt: its rooms' cores and scrap piles. The crypt is built one of {yaws} ways, so the panel gives the average of them, with the fewest and the most a crypt of that place can have. Your world holds one of those layouts.
loot.atPlay: Rolled when you take it. Chests, and what drops from things you break, are rolled by the game when you open or break them, not when the world is made. No map can know them; the panel gives the average the game's own odds give.

protector.title: The Helmet of the Protector never reaches the Forge of Potential
protector.why: The Forge of Potential lists a piece only when its recipe asks for an idol. Every other weapon and piece of armour that rises past its last level asks for one; the Helmet of the Protector does not: its recipe holds gold, its mould and moose hide, and nothing else.
protector.what: So the forge never offers it, and the helmet stays at level {max}, while the chest and legs of the same set rise further. Nothing you carry changes it: the forge reads the recipe, not your inventory.

events.title: Raids
events.question: What raids my base, and when does it stop?
events.answer: Every {minutes} minutes, while you are near a base, the game rolls a {chance}% chance of a raid from those your world has opened. A raid tied to the bosses comes only between one boss and the next, so killing the next one ends it for good.
events.how: Every other raid stays once opened. And you outlast a raid rather than clear it: each kind of creature keeps coming back up to the most it can have at once, a fresh one for each you kill, until the raid's time runs out.

invasion.title: The Jotun Invasion
invasion.text: This one is no raid on your base but an event of the world, and you start it yourself: break the Malicious Ice in the halls of a Mörkhalla in the Deep North and the Jotuns advance. Up to three stand at once, each a frozen patch of the Meadows, the Black Forest, the Swamp, the Mountain or the Plains, far from the world's centre and marked on your map; with no map, a trail of particles leads you to the nearest. Each holds until you break the Malicious Ice or the Orb of Fimbulvinter at its heart and the Jotuns retreat. Their own raid, the Jotuns at your base, begins once you have killed a Jotun and ends only with Kall Fimbulbringer.

trophies.title: Trophies
trophies.question: What is each trophy for?
trophies.answer: A boss's trophy goes back to the Sacrificial Stones: hung on its stone there, it gives you that boss's power. Every trophy stands under the first biome its creature lives in, with who drops it and what it goes into.

materials.title: Materials
materials.question: Where does it come from, and what is it for?
materials.answer: Each crafting material under the first biome that gives it: where you find it, and every recipe it goes into in any biome, so you know what to keep before a later biome asks for it. Gear, food, meads and trophies are on pages of their own.

note.piece_TrainingDummy: Every hit on it raises your weapon skill just as a hit on a creature does, so you can train at home in safety.

breakables.question: What is worth smashing?
breakables.answer: The Ashlands' pots, the one thing that breaks into silver; in the frost caves, the wooden gates for iron bars, the braziers for bronze and the hangings for Fenris hair; in the Mörkhalla, what drops hides, jute, chains and coins; and the Dvergr's furniture for scrap and surtling cores.
breakables.note: "Sometimes" means the object stands in a part of the place that some seeds build and others leave out.

group.ancientItems: An ancient item for the Forge of Potential

meads.title: Meads
meads.question: What does each mead do?
meads.lead: Every mead and potion by biome: what drinking it does and for how long, then what the mead ketill takes for its base. That cost buys several bottles, not one: the fermenter turns each base into a few.

hives.title: How many beehives a fermenter needs:
hives.text: a mead base takes {honey} honey, a hive makes one honey every {hive} seconds, and a fermenter turns a base every {ferment} seconds, so one fermenter that never stands idle takes {honey} × {hive} ÷ {ferment} = {hives} hives.

stations.title: Crafting stations
stations.question: What to build first?
stations.lead: A workbench, then a forge for bronze. A station levels up with the upgrades you build beside it, and better gear asks for a higher level, so plan the upgrades with the station: every station and upgrade by biome.

woodBuilding.title: Wood building
woodBuilding.question: What does a wooden house take?
woodBuilding.lead: A workbench within reach, then whatever each piece costs: every wooden wall, floor, roof, beam, door and stair the hammer raises by one, by biome.

stoneBuilding.title: Stone building
stoneBuilding.question: What does a stone house take?
stoneBuilding.lead: A stonecutter within reach, then whatever each piece costs: every stone, marble and grausten piece the hammer raises by one, by biome.

furniture.title: Furniture
furniture.question: What furniture can you build?
furniture.lead: Every bed, chair, table, chest, banner, rug and light the hammer builds, by biome. Before you fill a hall, check the comfort page: only the best piece of each kind counts toward your rest.

deepNorthBuilding.title: Deep North building
deepNorthBuilding.question: What does the hammer's Deep North tab hold?
deepNorthBuilding.lead: Roofs, walls and furniture that the game keeps apart from the wood and stone ones, with what each costs.

ships.title: Ships and carts
ships.question: Which ship to build?
ships.lead: The raft, the Karve, the Longship or the Drakkar, the cart and the siege engines: what each takes to build, by biome.

otherPieces.title: Other build pieces
otherPieces.question: What else does the hammer build?
otherPieces.lead: Portals, fires, stacks, piles, adornments, and the training dummy that trains your weapon skill at home, by biome.

wind.title: Wind
wind.question: Which way does the wind blow?
wind.answer: The world's clock decides it, not the seed: at the same hour of the same day the wind blows the same way in every world, so this table is your wind too.
wind.read: Each cell is where the wind comes from at the start of that game hour. The main direction holds for about {hold} minutes, with smaller turns every couple of minutes on top of it. The night's hours are grey: sleep through them and you never sail in them. The first hours of day 1 are empty, since a new world begins just before its first morning.
wind.dead: The sail is dead when the wind comes from within {deg}° of the bow, on either side, {share}% of all headings, and only the oars move you then. Moder's power turns the wind dead astern while it lasts: call it when the wind stands ahead of your beam. Her power is on

speedrun.stripMap: The world of the seed Valheim with the strip between two red lines
speedrun.stripCaption: The seed Valheim: the strip, {m} m wide between the two red lines, runs north and south through the start; the run keeps to it and leaves the rest alone.

dungeons.title: Caves and dungeons
dungeons.question: Which creatures live where?
dungeons.lead: Know what waits inside before you walk in: every cave, dungeon and camp that holds creatures, which stand there, how many, and how likely each is on your seed.

thing.piece_Charred_Balista: a Charred ballista, a turret that shoots

dungeon.title: Dungeons
dungeon.text: Behind the door your seed picks the rooms, and the rooms pick the creatures, so two dungeons of one kind need not hold the same foes.

camp.title: Camps
camp.text: Out in the open your seed lays out the huts and fences round a centre, and the creatures stand among them.

place.title: Caves and other places
place.text: Built the same every time. A creature that stands there only by chance was rolled once, when your world was made, so one that is missing never turns up later.

comfort.title: Comfort
comfort.question: How do I raise comfort?
comfort.lead: Rest under a roof by one piece of each kind: a fire, a bed, a chair, a table, a banner and the rest. Only the best piece of each kind counts, so a throne beside a chair adds only the throne.

rule.title: How comfort counts
rule.rested: Rested lasts {base} minutes at comfort 1, and {per} minute more for each level above it.
rule.sum: Comfort starts at {base}; a roof over you adds {shelter}. Then every piece within ten metres adds its comfort.
rule.groups: Pieces come in kinds: fires, beds, chairs, tables, banners, carpets, displays, decor, garlands, lanterns and leisure. Of each kind only the piece with the most comfort counts. A piece of no kind counts once, however many stand.
rule.lit: A fire counts only while it burns. An item stand is a display: it gives its comfort empty, and a trophy hung on it adds nothing.

byBiome.title: Comfort by biome
byBiome.text: How far your base's comfort climbs with what you can build by each biome: the best piece of each kind so far, plus every piece of no kind. Build all of it and comfort reaches {most}, and Rested lasts {minutes} minutes.

guides.title: Guides
guides.spreadLegend: The dark mark and the bold number: as a rule. The bar and the brackets: the middle half of seeds.
guides.meadows: How do I explore the Meadows? Meadows: a home on the shore, the first gear from boar and deer, the bees of the old houses, and Eikthyr's antlers.
guides.blackForest: How do I explore the Black Forest? Black Forest: copper and cores at its edge until you wear bronze or hide, then its towers, chambers and nests on the way to the Elder.
guides.bosses: How do I kill each boss? How to kill each boss: the hardest-hitting weapon you can make by then, the way round a straight fight, and the power its trophy gives.
guides.traders: What to buy from the traders? What to buy from the traders: everything Haldor, Hildir and the Bog Witch sell, and what each good is for.
guides.deepNorth: How do I explore the Deep North? Deep North: a camp in a village by Kall's gate, Bloodgold from the petrified trolls, the keys that open the Mörkhalla, the blood from the south, and Kall phase by phase.
guides.swamp: How do I explore the Swamp? Swamp: a camp on dry ground, the first iron from the nearest Sunken Crypt, then every crypt, the Abominations' roots and Bonemass.
guides.mountain: How do I explore the Mountain? Mountain: a climb on frost mead, the first silver into a wolf fur cape, then the drake nests and Moder.
guides.plains: How do I explore the Plains? Plains: a walled base by the sea, the smallest Fuling village for barley, flax and black metal, then the totems and Yagluth.
guides.mistlands: How do I explore the Mistlands? Mistlands: the Dvergr as allies, the Infested Mines for cores and the Sealbreaker, a Dvergr extractor for sap, and the Queen.
guides.ashlands: How do I explore the Ashlands? Ashlands: the Drakkar over the burning sea, a roofed foothold, the stone portal that carries metal, and the Charred Fortresses for Fader's bells.
guides.damage: What hurts each creature? Damage types: the weapon kind to bring against every creature and boss, and the resistance to wear against what it deals.
guides.weapons: Which weapon to use? Weapons: swords, axes, maces, knives, spears, atgeirs and fists by biome, what each is for and its damage.
guides.bows: Which bow and which arrows? Bows, crossbows and arrows: why the arrow sets the damage type, and every bow, bolt and bomb by biome.
guides.staffs: What does each staff cast? Staffs: what every staff fires, summons or lays on your allies, and what a cast costs in eitr and health.
guides.armour: Which armour to wear? Armour: helmets, chest and leg pieces, capes, shields and trinkets by biome.
guides.toolsCatalog: Which tools to make? Tools: pickaxes, the hammer, the hoe, the cultivator, saddles and fishing bait.
guides.events: What raids my base, and when does it stop? Raids: what opens each raid, what ends it, and who comes.
guides.forge: Can I upgrade my gear past its last level? Forge of Potential: where it stands, the idols, the odds, and why the answer is fixed.
guides.otherRules: How do I play with no death, no map or no portals? No death, no map, no portals: one thing taken from the usual game at a time, what each rule makes you plan for, and how the rules stack.
guides.speedrunnersStart: Is this seed worth the run? A speedrunner's start: what the starting island holds, the first loop from Eikthyr to Moder leg by leg, and the tests a seed must pass before you keep it.
guides.speedrun: How do I speedrun to the end? Speedrun: forge only what the next boss asks, let monsters chop and mine for you, and sail as little as you can.
guides.reverseRun: How do I play backwards, the Deep North first? Reverse run: a raft north, a camp by the Winding Tunnels, and the gates that send you south for Moder and Fader.
guides.whereToBuild: Where do I build the home I keep all game? Where to build your base: the open sea for the boat, how far each metal lies from home, which of them sail, where a bridge spares the voyage, and what the raids make of it.
guides.howMuchMetal: How much iron do I need? How much metal a run takes: the iron and silver of a full kit at top quality, the least the bosses' gates ask, and whether your seed holds it.
guides.hardcore: What does Very hard or the Hardcore preset change? Hard, Very hard and Hardcore: softer blows from you and harder ones from them, more stars, earlier raids, and the Hardcore death.
guides.bossArenas: How do I build a boss arena that nothing spawns into? Boss arenas: why walls count for nothing, the ring of fires and stations round the altar, and the nests no ring stops.
guides.taming: How do I tame an animal? Taming animals: who can be tamed and on what food, how to catch each one, breeding, and the three mounts.
guides.meads: What does each mead do? Meads: what each bottle does and for how long, and what its base costs at the mead ketill.
guides.trophies: What is each trophy for? Trophies: who drops it, what it goes into, and the power a boss's trophy gives at the Sacrificial Stones.
guides.stations: What to build first? Crafting stations: a workbench, then a forge, and every upgrade that levels them up.
guides.woodBuilding: What does a wooden house take? Wood building: every wall, floor, roof, beam, door and stair, and what each costs.
guides.stoneBuilding: What does a stone house take? Stone building: every stone, marble and grausten piece, and what each costs.
guides.furniture: What furniture can you build? Furniture: beds, chairs, tables, chests, banners, rugs and lights by biome.
guides.deepNorthBuilding: What does the hammer's Deep North tab hold? Deep North building: the roofs, walls and furniture the game keeps in a tab of their own.
guides.ships: Which ship to build? Ships and carts: the raft to the Drakkar, the cart and the siege engines, and what each takes.
guides.otherPieces: What else does the hammer build? Other build pieces: portals, fires, stacks and the training dummy.
guides.creatures: What does each creature drop, and what is it for? Creatures: health, weak spots, drops and the recipes they go into, by biome.
guides.dungeons: Which creatures live where? Caves and dungeons: who waits in each cave, dungeon and camp, and how likely on your seed.
guides.materials: Where does it come from, and what is it for? Materials: where to find each crafting material, and every recipe it goes into.
guides.breakables: What is worth smashing? What to break: the pots, gates, braziers, hangings and furniture that drop metal, hides, jute, chains, coins and moulds, and how often.
guides.farming: How do I farm? Farming: every crop, tree and vine the cultivator plants, what it is planted with, what it gives, how long it grows and where.
guides.comfort: How do I raise comfort? Comfort: the best piece of each kind, and how long Rested lasts.
guides.food: What to eat? Food and feasts: the best dishes for a melee fighter, an archer and a mage by each biome, and when to eat again.

meadows.title: Meadows
meadows.lead: What do I need from the Meadows? Eikthyr's antler, for the only pickaxe before bronze, and the beehives of the abandoned houses and the Draugr villages.

eikthyr.title: Eikthyr
eikthyr.summon: His altar takes {trophies} deer trophies: hunt deer on the way to it.
eikthyr.near: On half of all seeds the altar is within {median} m of the start; on nine seeds in ten within {most} m.
eikthyr.island: On {island}% of seeds it stands on the starting island; on the rest the first boat comes before the first boss.
eikthyr.power: Hang his trophy on the sacrificial stones at the start for his power: running and jumping cost less stamina, which carries half the game.
eikthyr.skip: Technically yes, but not on a run: without his antler there is no pickaxe, so no copper, no tin and no bronze, and without his power every run and jump costs full stamina.

pickaxe.title: The antler pickaxe
pickaxe.text: Eikthyr drops hard antlers. One antler and {wood} wood at a workbench make the antler pickaxe, the only pickaxe until bronze: it mines copper and tin.

bees.title: Beehives
bees.why: Beehives stand in the Meadows' abandoned houses, each house holding one at a {chance}% chance, and in the Draugr villages and farms, where several can stand together. A mead base takes {honey} honey, so a run takes three hives home for mead, four on a speedrun.
bees.far: The third nearest hive is usually {third} m from the start, the fourth {fourth} m.
bees.near: Within {reach} m of the start there are usually {near} hives.

wood.title: Fine wood by the start
wood.text: Fine wood comes only from birches and oaks. Within {reach} m of the start there are usually {groves} of them.
wood.earlyAxes: They want an axe of the bronze axe's tier, but the Early Axes get there without bronze: a Curious axe head and a Mysterious axe head, both from chests of the Meadows' abandoned houses, and wood at the workbench.

meadows.map: Every beehive, birch and oak of your seed is on the <link>Valheim seed map</link>, under Resources and Fine wood.
meadows.next: After Eikthyr the way goes into the Black Forest: <link>Black Forest</link>.

blackForest.title: Black Forest
blackForest.lead: What do I need from the Black Forest? Copper and tin for bronze, best from a troll cave by the shore, and the Elder's swamp key, which opens the Sunken Crypts.

reach.title: Getting there
reach.near: The start sits in a ring of Meadows: the nearest Black Forest is usually {median} m away, and rarely nearer than {least} m.
reach.island: On {island}% of seeds the starting island has Black Forest of its own.

bronze.title: Copper, tin and bronze
bronze.recipe: A bar of bronze is {copper} copper and {tin} tin at the forge. The bronze pickaxe takes {bars} bars and {coreWood} core wood: {allCopper} copper and {allTin} tin before the next pickaxe.
bronze.cave: Settle at a troll cave: the ledge at its mouth is flat ground, which the Black Forest rarely gives, and {veins} copper veins or more by the entrance are the sign to stop there.
bronze.caves: Of the {all} troll caves nearest the start, usually {caves} have that much copper by the entrance; the nearest of them is usually {nearest} m from the start.
bronze.tin: Tin grows only at the water's edge. Within {reach} m of that cave there are usually {tin} tin deposits, and the cave is usually {shore} m from the sea: copper and tin in one trip, and the boat at the door.
bronze.walk: The whole way of the first days, from the start by Eikthyr's altar to that cave, is usually {walk} m.
bronze.birches: Within {reach} m of it there are usually {birches} birches, for fine wood.

wood.title: Wood without an axe
wood.text: A troll fells trees, the birches and oaks of fine wood included, and mines copper, tin and even silver: lure it past them. The Elder's blows fell the plain trees round his altar, not the birches and oaks. Between them they cut the wood a run needs, so the axe can wait.

elder.title: The Elder
elder.summon: His altar takes {seeds} ancient seeds. Greydwarf nests drop them, and they stand in the Greydwarf camps of the Black Forest; a Greydwarf brute drops one now and then.
elder.near: On half of all seeds the altar is within {median} m of the start; on nine seeds in ten within {most} m.
elder.island: On {island}% of seeds it stands on the starting island.
elder.key: He drops the swamp key, which opens the door of a Sunken Crypt.
elder.skip: Yes, as everything in the game can be skipped: players tired of speedruns even play it in reverse, from the Deep North back to the Meadows. The cost is time and nerve: without his key the door of a Sunken Crypt stays closed to you.

haldor.title: Haldor
haldor.near: Haldor the trader lives in the Black Forest; his camp is usually {median} m from the start, and on {island}% of seeds on the starting island.

blackForest.map: Every troll cave, copper vein, tin deposit and birch of your seed is on the <link>Valheim seed map</link>, under Dungeons, Ore and Fine wood.

bosses.title: How to kill each boss
bosses.question: How do I kill each boss?
bosses.lead: Two ways for each, never only one: the weapon that hurts it most of what you can make by then, and the way players win without a straight fight, with fire where the boss burns. Under each, its health, its weaknesses, how long a campfire takes to burn it down and what its attacks deal; Kall phase by phase.

fire.time: a campfire alone burns it down in about {minutes} min, if it stays in the flames
fire.never: a campfire never kills it: it heals faster than the fire burns, or takes no fire

aspects.lead: He takes no damage from you in this phase. He brings back the {count} earlier bosses as aspects, at most {atOnce} at a time, Eikthyr's first; each aspect's death strikes him for {blast}, so all must die. An aspect's health is its own (that of {health}), but each takes damage just as its boss does, and blunt is never weaker than full on any of them: what hurts each is in

bosses.breaks: They fell trees and break rock

direct.title: The straight fight
direct.text: What you can make by the {biome} that hits it hardest, one hit counted after its weaknesses and resistances; a bow with the best arrow of the time, a crossbow with the best bolt:

power.title: The power of the trophy
power.how: Hang the trophy on its stone at the Sacrificial Stones: once you call the power it lasts {minutes} min, and you can call it again after {cooldown} min.
power.sail: The wind follows the world's clock, not your course: it holds a main direction for about {windHoldMin} min and is as likely behind you as ahead. A sail dies when the wind comes from within {sailDeadDeg}° of the bow on either side, {sailDeadShare}% of all headings, and then you row. Her power turns the wind dead astern whatever your heading, so call it when the wind stands ahead of your beam; with the wind already behind or abeam it gains you nothing.
power.sailMore: Where the wind comes from, hour by hour all year, is in the tool
power.none: The game gives no power for this trophy.

tip.Dragon: She fights in the air and lands only now and then, so bring a bow. The table ranks poison arrows first because it counts a hit's whole damage, but poison trickles in over a few seconds; fire, which she is weak to, lands at once, so fire arrows serve as well.

other.title: The other way
other.Eikthyr: Circle the big rocks round his altar and shoot from behind them: the rocks stop his charge, though not his stomp.
other.gd_king: Ring his platform and the gaps between the pillars with campfires: fire hurts him double, and he burns as he walks over them while you shoot from behind a pillar. Or dig under the altar: its platform is a roof he cannot break, room for a workbench and a portal.
other.Bonemass: Shoot him from above, from a stone tower or a high tree, with frost arrows; level the ground round the altar with a hoe first, so you can move and leeches keep away.
other.Dragon: Dig a trench against the side of her summoning platform, which cannot be broken, and stay in it: when she lands, her breath and claws do not reach you, and you shoot straight up. Bring a lot of arrows.
other.GoblinKing: Speedrunners circle him: stay close, keep running round to his back from the first blow to the last, and he turns too slowly to hit you. If you would rather shoot, keep a stone pillar between you and him and step out to fire: breaking his line of sight stops his beam.
other.SeekerQueen: The vestibule at her entrance is safe: she does not attack you there and nothing spawns there, so build your rest and repairs just outside.
other.Fader: Summon two trolls with the Trollstav and stay out of his reach: he fights them and leaves you alone while you do not hit him. Or dig two pits side by side and leave the ground between them as the wall, never a built one: he breaks pieces, not earth, and when he cannot reach you it is a piece he goes for. Line his pit with Ashwood stakewalls: they hurt him, but each wears out after a few hits and breaks when he walks into it, so keep repairing them from your side. Nothing can be dug by his altar: lead him out of his arena to the pits first.
other.FrozenKing: Fight each phase with what it is open to. The first and the third take half from pierce, fire, frost and lightning, so bows, spears and staffs do half: bring the heaviest blunt or slash weapon you have, and expect no stagger and no opening in either. In the second, leave him be and kill the aspects as they come: blunt hurts every one in full, the Elder's and Moder's burn, and Bonemass's and Yagluth's shrug off pierce.

traders.title: What to buy from the traders
traders.question: What to buy from the traders?
traders.answer: Haldor's Megingjord and his extra inventory rows carry more of every haul; the Bog Witch's serving tray and spices turn your cooking into feasts; Hildir sells clothes and hats, more of them with every chest you bring her back.

about.Haldor: He trades in the Black Forest: gear and the extra inventory rows, with more on his shelf as the bosses fall.
about.BogWitch: She trades in the Swamp, in what your cooking and potions need: the serving tray for feasts, each biome's spice and the ingredients of meads.
about.Hildir: She trades in the Meadows, in clothes and hats, and puts out more each time you bring back one of her chests.

sell.title: What the traders buy
sell.text: These are all a trader will buy, each for a fixed number of coins. A few also go into recipes, so think before you sell them; the rest are good for nothing but coins, and coins are good for nothing but the goods above.

quest.title: Hildir's quest
quest.text: Hildir is the only trader with a quest. Three of her chests were stolen, and each now lies in a dungeon of its own: kill its guard and the chest drops. Every chest you bring her back puts more of her goods on sale.

traders.writhan: One of her goods waits on a kill instead of a chest: the Crown of Roots goes on sale only after you kill a Writhan, a rare creature of the Swamp and no boss.

essential.title: Speedrunners: what is the least I must buy?
essential.text: A race buys only these and walks past every other shelf: together they cost {coins} coins, and a runner who has them needs no more.

row.spices: A spice for each biome's feast

for.spices: No feast without its biome's spice; each goes on sale after that biome's boss.

deepNorth.title: Deep North
deepNorth.lead: What to bring to the Deep North? The Grappling Hook and the Feather cape, both made in the Mistlands: the hook climbs, the cape falls without harm.

hook.title: The Grappling Hook
hook.recipe: Its recipe appears when you pick up a Hook from a Dvergr chest in an Infested Mine. It takes {yggdrasil} Yggdrasil wood, {eitr} refined eitr, {mandibles} mandibles and {hooks} Hook at the black forge.
hook.use: It pulls you up the Mistlands' cliffs and into the raised entrance of a Deep North tower, and up a floor when mobs close in.

cape.title: The Feather cape
cape.recipe: {feathers} feathers, {scaleHide} scale hide and {eitr} refined eitr at the Galdr Table.
cape.use: It slows a fall so a misstep costs nothing: jump down inside a tower instead of crossing it. It burns easily, so keep it away from fire.

tower.title: Mörkhalla
tower.text: The Deep North's tower. An Intricate Key, used up at the door, opens it; the key's mould lies in the Winding Tunnels under the abandoned villages.

reverse.title: Starting in the Deep North
reverse.text: Nothing stops a ship from sailing there first, and the biome appears only in ground nobody has explored. But its progress needs embers from Fader, the Ashlands' boss, so a run that starts in the north still comes back south for them.

swamp.lead: What does the Swamp give? Iron, from the scrap piles of the Sunken Crypts, which only the Elder's key opens; Bonemass, summoned with withered bones, drops the wishbone that finds silver.

crypts.title: Sunken Crypts
crypts.a: Iron comes from the muddy scrap piles inside the crypts. The door takes the key the Elder drops.
crypts.b: Surtlings near the crypts give the cores a smelter and a charcoal kiln need, so a crypt with fire holes by it saves a trip.

bonemass.title: Bonemass
bonemass.a: His altar takes withered bones, found in the crypts. He is weak to blunt damage: a mace, from a raised platform with a roof.
bonemass.b: His wishbone points to silver ore buried in the mountains. A run can skip him and dig the mountains long enough to find silver without it.

danger.title: Poison and water
danger.a: Blobs and leeches poison; a poison resistance mead makes the swamp bearable.

swamp.title: Swamp

mountain.lead: What does the Mountain give? Silver, found with Bonemass's wishbone and mined with an iron pickaxe; Moder's altar takes three drake eggs from the nests on the cliffs.

cold.title: Cold
cold.a: The cold hurts without frost resistance: a wolf cape or a frost resistance mead.

silver.title: Silver
silver.a: Silver lies under the snow; the wishbone sounds over it and an iron pickaxe mines it.

moder.title: Moder
moder.a: Her altar takes drake eggs from the nests on the mountain; best is a mountain that holds both. She is weak to fire: bonfires round the place she lands.
moder.b: Her drop lets the player sail against the wind.

mountain.title: Mountain

plains.lead: What do the Plains give? Black metal and the Fulings' totems from their villages, and barley and flax for bread and linen; Yagluth's altar takes five totems.

villages.title: Fuling villages
villages.a: Fuling villages hold black metal scrap, totems, and barley and flax growing wild: the seeds of the Plains' farm.
villages.b: Deathsquitos strike from the air; a block or a shield handles them.

yagluth.title: Yagluth
yagluth.a: His altar takes five Fuling totems, so a run clears villages near it.

plains.title: Plains

mistlands.lead: What do the Mistlands give? Black marble, Yggdrasil wood and eitr; the Infested Mines hold the Queen's way in and the Hook for the Grappling Hook.

terrain.title: Cliffs and mist
terrain.a: The ground is cliffs under mist. The Feather cape removes fall damage and the Grappling Hook climbs, both made here.

soldier.title: The Seeker Soldier
soldier.a: Its blows break black marble and Yggdrasil shoots, which otherwise want black metal tools: stand so it hits them for you.

queen.title: The Queen
queen.a: Her roar calls Seekers and brood; keep the pillars between you and her.

mistlands.title: Mistlands

ashlands.lead: What do the Ashlands give? Flametal and ashwood; Fader, summoned with three bells, drops the embers the Deep North needs.

lava.title: Lava
lava.a: Lava runs over the ground away from the biome's edges; the map shows it.

fader.title: Fader
fader.a: His altar takes three bells. The Ashwood stakewall pierces whatever touches it.

morgen.title: Morgen
morgen.a: Morgen's blows break trees and rock of the Ashlands.

ashlands.title: Ashlands

weapons.title: Weapons
weapons.question: Which weapon to use?
weapons.lead: A sword when you attack, a mace when you hold your ground, and the mace again on the hardest settings, where it is the favourite; an atgeir against crowds, a knife from the shadows, fists if they are your style. Every one by biome, with its damage, station and materials.
weapons.damageLink: Before you choose, see which damage type hurts your next foe most, and what it hits back with, on
weapons.staffsLink: What each staff casts is on

damage.title: Damage types
damage.question: What hurts each creature?
damage.lead: Every creature and boss by biome: the damage types it takes harder or softer, so you know which weapon kind to bring, and the damage it deals back, so you know which resistance to wear.

hurts.title: What hurts each creature
hurts.lead: A weak spot multiplies the hit, a resistance divides it. Each weapon kind deals mostly one type:
hurts.fire: Fire is the weakness you meet most often: in the Black Forest and the Mountain most creatures take it harder, which is why speedrunners burn them with campfires. Drop the habit at the Mistlands: there and in the Ashlands no creature is weak to fire, and in the Ashlands most resist it.

deals.title: What each creature hits with
deals.lead: The strongest blow of each damage type a creature can deal, before your armour: wear the resistance to its type.
deals.pierce: Pierce is what the bosses hit you with, all but Bonemass and Yagluth, and the Deathsquito of the Plains stings with nothing else. The Root Harnesk is the one chest piece that halves pierce, so wear it against them; it takes fire harder, though, so leave it at home for Yagluth. Every armour piece is on

bows.title: Bows, crossbows and arrows
bows.question: Which bow and which arrows?
bows.lead: The arrow, not the bow, sets the damage type: a bow's damage adds to its arrow's, so fire arrows for what burns, frost for what freezes. Every bow, crossbow, arrow, bolt and bomb by biome.

staffs.title: Staffs
staffs.question: What does each staff cast?
staffs.lead: Elemental staffs deal the damage themselves and cost only eitr: a fireball that bursts where it lands, a stream of frost, a volley of lightning, roots that rise and strike. Blood magic staffs put something between you and the enemy, and take a share of your health with the eitr: they raise skeletons, a troll or animal spirits, or lay a shield on you and your allies; the Echo Spike alone strikes for itself and asks no health. A summoning staff is the one worth upgrading first, since every level of it lets one more summon stand. Every staff by biome, with what a cast does and costs.
staffs.eitr: You have no eitr at all until you eat for it, and a staff without eitr casts nothing: the dishes that give it are on

armour.title: Armour
armour.question: Which armour to wear?
armour.lead: Every helmet, chest piece, leg piece, cape, shield and trinket by biome, with its armour, block and effects. Mind the speed as well as the armour: some pieces slow you more than usual for their kind, and a few make you faster.

toolsCatalog.title: Tools
toolsCatalog.question: Which tools to make?
toolsCatalog.lead: Pickaxes, the hammer, the hoe and the cultivator, torches and lanterns, saddles and fishing bait, by biome.

creatures.title: Creatures
creatures.question: What does each creature drop, and what is it for?
creatures.lead: Hunt with a recipe in mind: every creature by biome, its health, what hurts it, what it drops and every recipe each drop goes into.
creatures.phases: Health: {first}, {second} and {third}, one phase after another; how he fights each is on
creatures.mapBefore: Where it stands on your seed: its spawners on the
creatures.chops: Its blows fell trees up to tool tier {tier} ({damage} chopping).
creatures.mines: Its blows break rock and ore up to tool tier {tier} ({damage} mining).

sets.note: Kills of this creature without stars, on average, for its own drops alone; a starred one drops more, so it takes fewer.
sets.runsOut: Not every kill can come from its places: each gives at most {n}, once a world.
sets.runsOutRooms: Not every kill can come from its places: each gives it once a world.

sources.respawns: spawners that bring it back {minutes} minutes after the last one is gone
sources.areas: nests that keep spawning while they stand
sources.openEvery: the open {biomes}, a {chance}% chance every {minutes} minutes
sources.fixed: Its places give a fixed number, {n} a place, once a world; the rest come from {rest}.
sources.fixedRooms: Its places give a fixed number, once a world; the rest come from {rest}.
sources.runsOut: It runs out: its places give it once a world, and nothing brings it back.
sources.nightOnly: It comes only at night and leaves at dawn.
sources.nightMore: More of it come at night.
sources.starsAtNight: At night it can have more stars.
sources.starsFrom: In the open world it has stars only beyond {m} m from the world's centre.

stars.title: Stars
stars.text: A star means more health, harder hits and more drops. Each star is a roll, mostly at {chance}% (nests and a few spawners differ), rolled again for the second; a few creatures roll only far from the world's centre, and a night spawn may allow more stars than the day's. A raid's creatures come without stars, except the Ticks and the escorts of Hildir's guards. Your world's settings and some biome patches change the chance.

head.share: Of those that can have two

stars.note: Drops: both the chance and the amount of each drop.

fish.title: Fishing
fish.text: Haldor sells the rod and plain bait; every other bait is plain bait and a trophy, so the creatures you hunt decide which fish you can catch. Every fish goes into raw fish, and that is what the dishes take.
fish.where: {biomes}, in water {water} m deep or more

notes.Troll: A troll cave often holds a troll inside and sometimes one more by its entrance; neither comes back once killed. One troll in {weaponSets} carries a log: it reaches farther but never throws, while an unarmed troll punches, slams and hurls rocks from afar; otherwise they are the same troll, with the same health and drops. Kill a troll and the Elder, and trolls can raid your base. Pierce hurts them most, so bring a spear or arrows. They break walls, so no trap holds one, but lure one past trees and copper and it fells and mines for you.
notes.Bjorn: Wall a bear in on flat ground with a campfire under it and it burns; keep repairing the fire and the walls while it does.
notes.GoblinBruteBros: When Thungr falls, Zil rises from him and fights on; Zil carries Hildir's Bronze Chest.
notes.GoblinShaman_Hildir: No spawner makes him: he rises when Thungr falls, in Hildir's Plains fortress.
notes.Serpent: A sea monster: it hunts ships in the deep ocean.
notes.BonemawSerpent: A sea monster: it hunts ships in the waters of the Ashlands.

farming.title: Farming
farming.question: How to farm?
farming.lead: Every crop, tree and vine the cultivator plants: what it is planted with, what it gives, how long it grows and where it grows.
farming.cultivator: The cultivator turns ground into a field and plants. A crop grows only on cultivated ground and only in the biomes listed beside it; a seed from one biome often grows in others, but not always where it was found.

crops.title: Crops
crops.text: A crop is planted with its seed and gives its harvest. Where the seeds do not come back with it, plant one of the harvest (or a seed, for kale) and it grows into seeds: one find keeps a field going. What each harvest goes into is on its row in
crops.conclusion: The {biome} grow {count} of the {all} crops, every one but {missing}: the one farm that feeds a whole game. Some grow in one biome only, {only}: no home elsewhere grows them, so they are farmed where they grow. Your home in the Meadows grows {home} of them.
crops.sameTime: Every crop takes the same {min}–{max} minutes, so a field is chosen by where it grows, not by how fast.

trees.title: Trees
trees.text: A sapling grows on any ground; what a grown tree gives when felled is its average.
trees.conclusion: The {most} is the slow one, {min}–{max} minutes, and pays for it with {fine} fine wood, more than any other tree: plant oaks where you will stay. For wood you burn and build with in bulk the {quick} is back within {quickMax} minutes.

vines.title: Vines
vines.text: Vines grow fastest of all and give vineberries.
vines.conclusion: A vine is ripe in {min}–{max} minutes, a crop in {crop} at the least: a few vines by the door keep the vineberries coming while a field is still green.

where.title: Where should I farm?
where.text: In the {biome}, once you can hold ground there: one farm grows nearly everything the game plants, so it is the field you keep to the end. Until then farm at home, where {home} of the {all} crops grow. What each crop then feeds is on

food.title: Food and feasts
food.question: What to eat?
food.answer: Health dishes for a melee fighter, stamina dishes for an archer, eitr dishes for a mage; a feast fills one slot with all three.
food.basics: You eat up to three different dishes at once; each raises health, stamina or eitr and regenerates health while it lasts.

who.title: Who eats what
who.matrix: The three best dishes of each kind you can make by the end of each biome: eat all three, since different dishes always stack. A dish in bold is new in that biome; the others are still the best of an earlier one.
who.againText: a dish can be eaten again once half its time has passed, and it still gives about four fifths of its value then. Eat each again at its half and the three slots stay nearly full.
who.notYet: No dish of this kind before the biome where the row starts: eitr food begins in the Mistlands, with magic.
who.feastText: health and stamina, and eitr from the Mistlands on, in one slot and for the longest time.

feasts.title: Feasts
feasts.text: Make a feast at the food preparation table and set it down on a serving tray, and the whole group eats from it.
feasts.tray: Buy the serving tray from the Bog Witch.
